sentences.text:
In this petition, petitioner seeks the following reliefs;
"a) Issue an appropriate order and quash the First Information Report in Crime No.20/2024 filed by the 1st respondent-Robertson Pet Police station, Kolar District at KGF, against the petitioner, which is submitted before Senior Civil Judge &
Principal JMFC Court, Kolar District at KGF registered for an alleged offence punishable under Section 420, 465, 468, 471 read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code,
M. Rajendra vs State Of Karnataka on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92668177/
2 to secure the ends of justice and to prevent abuse of process of Court.
NC: 2025:KHC:18927 HC-KAR (b) Pass such other orders, as the petitioner is entitled to in the facts and circumstances of the case,
in the interest of justice and equity."

sentences.text:
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 and learned counsel for respondent No.2 and perused the material on record.
3.

A perusal of the material on record will indicate that on 30.01.2024, the General Power of Attorney alleged to have been executed by respondent No.2 in favour of accused No.1 - K.A. Anand is said to have come into existence, on the basis of which, Sale Deed dated 01.02.2024 is alleged to have been executed by accused No.1-K.A. Anand in his own favour.

Subsequently, on 13.02.2024,
respondent No.2 - de facto complainant filed the complaint, which was registered as FIR in Crime No.20/2024 against accused No.2-petitioner, who is an Advocate and Notary as well as against accused No.1- K.A. Anand for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 420, 465, 468, 471 read with 34 of IPC.
Aggrieved by the impugned proceedings, the petitioner-accused No.2 is before this Court by way of the present petition.
NC: 2025:KHC:18927 HC-KAR 4.

A perusal of the material on record, in particular, the complaint, will indicate that except vague,
general, bald and omnibus allegations against the petitioner by alleging that the General Power of Attorney was created by accused No.1- K.A.Anand in collusion with the petitioner, no other allegations or specific material particulars are forthcoming in the impugned complaint and the FIR.

In addition thereto, respondent No.2 has not taken recourse to the mandatory procedure prescribed under Section 13 of the Notaries Act, 1952, as held by this Court in the case of H.R. Ramamurthy vs.
K. Raju1.
5.

It is also relevant to state that in addition to the impugned complaint lodged by respondent No.2,
the petitioner himself has lodged one more complaint as against accused No.1-K.A. Anand, which is registered as FIR on 17.02.2024.

Under these circumstances, in the absence of the complaint and the FIR disclosing commission of offence by the petitioner- accused No.2, I am of the considered opinion that continuation of the impugned proceedings qua the petitioner-accused No.2 Crl.P.No.9451/2017, DD 21.02.2023.
NC: 2025:KHC:18927 HC-KAR would amount to abuse of process of law warranting interference in the present petition.

6. In the result, the following;
